content: If you experience side effects while using pantoprazole, it is important to contact your doctor for medical advice. Before starting this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to pantoprazole, similar drugs (such as lansoprazole or omeprazole), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Some symptoms may indicate a more serious underlying condition. Proton pump inhibitors, including pantoprazole, may increase the risk of bone fractures, particularly with prolonged use, higher doses, or in older adults. Older individuals may also be more sensitive to side effects such as bone loss and fractures. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if absolutely necessary, as it passes into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Always maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share this with your doctor and pharmacist. Certain medications require stomach acid for proper absorption, and pantoprazole reduces stomach acid, which may affect how well these products work. Additionally, pantoprazole may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as urine tests for THC or blood tests for specific tumors, potentially leading to false results. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms like loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. In the U.S., you can call 1-800-222-1222. While using this medication, your doctor may order lab tests, such as magnesium blood tests, to monitor your health. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Different brands of this medication may have specific storage requirements. Refer to the product packaging or consult your pharmacist for proper storage instructions. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information tailored to your specific health needs.
